ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a benzo-fused five-membered imide-like skeleton, with a fused benzene ring on the left; there is one nitrogen atom in the five-membered ring, and the nitrogen atom is connected rightward to a methylene, then connected to a carbonyl, the other end of which is labeled R. There is a carbonyl below the five-membered ring; the top ring carbon is simultaneously connected to an OMe group and a negatively charged oxygen, and there are also curved arrows in the figure but the problem asks to ignore them. Reasoning: According to the specified method, only transcribe the atomic connectivity, take the variable R as the wildcard *, which is connected to the side-chain carbonyl carbon, and the side chain is written as *C(=O)C. This methylene is then connected to the ring nitrogen, written as N1. The fused benzo-imide part is encoded as N1C(=O)c2ccccc2C1, and the top ring carbon is further given [O-] and OC substituents, giving *C(=O)CN1C(=O)c2ccccc2C1([O-])OC.

method.method_draft: Ignore all curved-arrow annotations and transcribe only atom connectivity. Start from the variable R substituent as '*' attached to the side-chain carbonyl carbon, write the side chain as *C(=O)C, connect that methylene to the imide nitrogen as N1, encode the cyclic imide/fused benzene portion as N1C(=O)c2ccccc2C1, then add the substituents on the top ring carbon as ([O-])OC. Combining these fragments gives *C(=O)CN1C(=O)c2ccccc2C1([O-])OC.
